enquiry: We are developing a hot polymer extrusion process that incorporates an active pharmaceutical ingredient. We want to investigate whether an optical measurement can detect composition changes while the melt is being processed. We have offline assays, but the process interface is hot and may be exposed to material build up. We need an initial comparison plan and the questions required before choosing a probe.

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today with composition control during extrusion, and what decision would real-time data drive (e.g. adjusting feed, rejecting material)?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the decision the optical measurement must support and the acceptable response time.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Decision unknown; the first step is a feasibility study on whether composition change is detectable at all.

clarification_questions.question: What is the target API and its expected concentration range in the melt, stated as ppm or %, and what composition change must be detected?
clarification_questions.why: The concentration level decides whether NIR or another method can reach the required sensitivity.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Level unknown; lab screening establishes whether the API is at ppm or % level before any method is chosen.

clarification_questions.question: What is the polymer and formulation, and is the melt clear, turbid or opaque at the measurement point?
clarification_questions.why: Optical properties decide the probe geometry (transmission, diffuse reflection or ATR) and whether the API signal can be seen through the polymer.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Optical state unknown; lab screening on representative melt samples determines the probe geometry.

clarification_questions.question: What are the melt temperature, pressure, screw and die configuration, and how much do the material texture, particle size, bubbles or homogeneity vary during the run?
clarification_questions.why: Temperature and sample variation affect spectra and calibration; they also limit the probe materials that can be used.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Process conditions unknown; the lab screening must cover the temperature range of the process as stated by the client.

clarification_questions.question: Where would the probe be installed (barrel, die or melt pipe), what is the distance from the measuring point to the analyzer, and are any optical fibers already installed?
clarification_questions.why: Fiber type limits the usable wavelength range, and remote measurement changes the choice between NIR silica fibers and mid-IR fibers.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Installation point and distance unknown; the comparison plan assumes a remote analyzer is needed until the layout is known.

clarification_questions.question: How is material build-up at the interface handled today, and what cleaning or sterilization routine is applied to the probe interface?
clarification_questions.why: Build-up on the window or ATR tip changes the signal and the probe design, and cleaning requirements exclude some probe materials.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Build-up tolerance unknown; the probe must be assumed to need a cleaning-compatible design, and fouling is tested during the in-line trial.

clarification_questions.question: Which offline assay is used as the reference for API content, what is its accuracy and sampling frequency, and how are reference samples taken from the melt?
clarification_questions.why: Spectra and reference values must be time-aligned, and the reference accuracy sets the achievable model accuracy.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method unknown; the comparison plan requires a reference assay with known accuracy before any model is built.

clarification_questions.question: Are existing spectroscopic data or calibrations available from earlier formulations or lab work, and would they be reused for this polymer and API?
clarification_questions.why: Chemometric calibrations are matrix-specific, so reuse for a changed formulation can invalidate them.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No existing calibration assumed; any model is built new on this formulation.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and budget are required, and is the setting a production line, a pilot line or a research laboratory?
clarification_questions.why: These decide whether a simple few-wavelength sensor or a full-spectrum system is the right scale-up path.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; the plan starts with lab screening and keeps the sensor choice open until they are stated.

clarification_questions.question: What regulatory or quality framework applies to the product (e.g. GMP or other pharmaceutical standards), and what must be documented for the measurement?
clarification_questions.why: Regulatory context decides the validation effort and the robustness and documentation needed for scale-up.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Framework unknown; the scale-up step will need a check of applicable standards before any in-line use.

flags_before_revision.detail: not_supported: The claim says "Diffuse reflection samples only 0.5-1 mm" as a general rule. The cited table rows give 0.5-1 mm only for the NIR diffuse reflection probe on scattering media and powders. The integrating sphere is 5-10 mm and surface-at-distance is 2-5 mm. The claim also applies the figure to a hot polymer melt, which the pages do not cover. Fix: Restrict the figure to the NIR diffuse reflection probe row (0.5-1 mm, scattering media/powder) and state that the depth for a polymer melt is not given in the sources.

not_supported: The cited pages give the ATR depth of 1-6 um and the PIR fibre range of 3-17 um. They do not say that contact and fouling dominate for ATR, and they do not say that mid-IR requires PIR fibre (the fibre table only lists PIR as one option). Fix: Keep the 1-6 um depth. State fouling and contact as a risk to assess, not a finding, and say that PIR fibre is one option for mid-IR transmission, not a requirement.

not_supported: The cited pages list NIR diffuse reflection probes for scattering media and powders. They do not show that such a probe is suitable for a polymer melt. The example at the die (S02 p.14) that would support this is not cited. Fix: Cite S02 p.14 for the NIR probe at the die and mark the suitability for the melt as an assumption to test.

not_supported: DOCX §5 lists contact and fouling as a limitation of the MIR ATR method. It does not say that build-up on a probe window or tip changes the NIR signal or that a cleaning-compatible design is needed. Fix: Attribute fouling to the ATR contact case, or cite a source that describes build-up on NIR probe windows.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
insufficient_information_is_valid: If the known facts cannot justify a method choice, say so, ask the deciding questions and propose the next step. [DOCX §3]
